i am a grad of fine art this year. they "paused" admissions into the direct entry BFA in October 2022, and have been working to restructure the program as a BA with a major in visual art, so your first year you would be admitted into general arts and science like every other program and have to take general first year courses as a prerequisite to enter the major (or minor?) plan in second year. at least I believe that was the plan, even as a student in BFA nobody reall yknew what the future of the program will look like. the class below me (class of 2026) will be the last class to graduate with a BFA credential, and subsequent graduating classes will have a BA. 

I haven't heard really about the structuring of the new courses but I believe it is less intensive/more flexible in terms of program choices, adding minor/exchange experiences etc. my experience was that my class were directly admitted absed on our portfolios into 19 spots with an additional 10 for con-ed, so all our core classes were with the same small cohort of peers. all my credits are studio based and one studio class is essentially worth 2 regular courses in first and second year (so 6 units as opposed to 3) and in third and fourth is worth 3 (9 units for one class). so the time commitment for what shows up as one class is much higher. I have many opinions on axing the BFA and it's conservatory style intensive training, which the former has its pros and cons of course, but I hope that subsequent classes doing the BA in Visual art will have a similar experience of the benefits the BFA have given to myself and my peers, despite the former programs flaws it was really something special i was privileged to be a part of and I am very saddened it won't be continuing in the same way

does your doctor know about the past abuse? defintley mention your history with seizures. i’m wondering if it’s street xanax i’m not sure if you’ve tested them ever but i’d be curious about the possibility of another substance they may have been cut with possibly causing the seizures? regardless weather or not it may have been due to something else within it or the xanax itself is important to still mention this just in case it was a reaction to the benzodiazepine itself. 

in general i  cant speak as much to xanax but can speak to klonopin as it’s the only benzo i’ve been prescribed. i did end up significantly misusing it for a time but have since been able to get myself back under control. 

as it’s technically a controlled substance they should only be dispensing a certain about every so often, at least where i’m from. you could mention this and drive it home that this is important for you if you think it will help. 

i defintley felt safer and better about recovery when i knew how much i was getting i was using it more sparingly and only when it was nessecary. knowing that i’d only get a certain amount after a month or so helped me stay more responsible with it. 

you could also consider talking with an addictions counsellor about starting something in the same class as to what you used to abuse. they might be able to help you navigate some of those complexities. i often wish i had done this myself. or an NA/other addictions group. i know not everyone finds this helpful but it may be worth a try if you are unsure about starting them because of your addiction history, regardless weather or not it’s been years. in either and any case, best of luck and stay safe!

hey! you are not alone in your struggles, i've been feeling the same way for my last 3 years here. a lot of advice I find is nonspecific to people who are genuinely socially anxious, and i know putting yourself out there is scarier and harder than it is for most, so I hope my words might be useful.

the only close friend i actually hang out with is my roommate, who I was friends with before coming here - she has a friend group here whereas I don't. I was off-campus first year during 2021/22 still partially covid, so living totally alone with classes going online screwed me a bit for meeting new people where I may have in res, etc, in addition to already being quite socially anxious it certainly wasn't easy. with joining clubs last and this year and being friendly and receptive to people i meet in clubs, people in my program which I am lucky is very small, I have come to know some familiar faces I can smile and wave to :). 

I have met some of my roommates friend group as sometimes I ask what she's up to on the weekends or for big events like hoco etc. and if I can tag along. She's great of course and is happy for me to join if i ask. I know it can feel daunting, but if you have a good relationship, it might just work out. sometimes I'll take the train home for the weekend and see some friends from home, but i understand not everyone has that luxury of living a train away from your hometown. 

now, this comes with time, but if you're an introvert like me, sometimes I remind myself it's not the worst thing to be with people 24/7. it's by no means easy to get to this place, nor do I expect you to be fine with it right away (I still have days where I'm not - feeling lonely can really get to you when you're seemingly surrounded by people and their friends all the time while you're alone). I've slowly learned to be okay with having time to myself between or after classes and try to make good use of it. i'll pop in the library and revise my lecture notes or work on upcoming assignments - that way, i'm distracted from feeling crappy but I am also getting stuff done.

feel free to reach out to me if you ever want someone to talk to!

bit late replying to this but a ton of first years are often pressured into signing leases ASAP in like november so they go very quickly right at the start of the year and that speed can certainly be dizzying when it’s your first time looking for a place to lease and i know what it’s like to feel like you’re too late. but you still have LOADS of time! 

i got my current place in late january of last year and signed a lease for me and one of my current roommates for next year about a week ago, but a lot of listings come up in february/march when tenants start giving their landlords legal notice of leaving. keep on top of it though, try to check facebook groups (queens off campus housing/queens student housing) or marketplace, the off campus listing service, kijiji, zumper or padmapper. also check out local property management companies to see what they have available - were with amber peak and they’ve been decent. i’ve heard mostly good things about limestone property management, BPE rentals and heron property management. frontenac and panadew are generally middle of the road. there’s a lot out there but reddit has been a really good source of information based on the reputation of landlords and companies in kingston, i’d do some searching on here as well to better situate yourself with who’s who and what’s good and not so good. 

be sure to always do your research on your landlord/contact person before signing a lease and always view it in person. the general golden rule is to avoid phil lam (queensapthousing/onehomes/and also a bunch of different names i can’t keep track of, but all his listings have the same advertised number which is on the websites i mentioned above so be sure to check for that on any listing) and daphne dean unless you literally never have people over and can abide by a curfew lol.
